- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often overcorrects upward; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is > 85 and true outcome drops below 75, apply 5–10% downward correction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations (e.g., 1.00 → -0.33 → 0.33), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by 1–2% per cycle.
